stories.description: Democrats look all but certain to take the US House. The real fight is for the Senate, where a handful of races in states Republicans never expected to defend will decide who controls Washington.
stories.excerpt: Polling stations are opening across the United States in a midterm election that, a year ago, Republicans expected to survive with their Senate majority intact. That expectation has been reduced to a hope. Start with the House of Representatives, where the question is no longer whether Democrats win, but by how much. Prediction markets give them a 95% chance of taking control. The Cook Political Report now rates 222 seats as at least leaning Democratic, four more than the 218 needed for a majority, against 195 for Republicans, with 18 pure toss-ups. A good night for Democrats could see them controlling as many as 230 seats. A great night means the Senate and a blue wave. Republicans hold 53 of the Senate's 100 seats. Tehran’s reported seven conditions begin with a ceasefire across the Middle East. They also include the release of Iranian assets frozen abroad and the lifting of sanctions on Iran’s oil sector. stories.title: Scientists say they’ve found the strongest evidence yet of red blood cells in a dinosaur bone
stories.description: A new study found chemical evidence of red blood cells in a 115 million-year-old dinosaur bone, offering new clues about how biological material can survive.
stories.excerpt: Traces of prehistoric blood could reveal unprecedented clues about dinosaur biology, but they’ve been notoriously difficult to confirm. Now, researchers studying a 115 million-year-old dinosaur bone say they’ve found the strongest evidence yet of red blood cells in a fossil. Tissues, cells and other soft biological samples rarely ever survive the fossilization process and thus make for controversial discoveries. A few previous studies, dating back to the late 1990s, have reported structures resembling red blood cells in dinosaur and other reptile fossils, but researchers have fiercely debated their legitimacy. The new study, published Monday in the journal Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, used a combination of new microscopic imaging and chemical analyses to find not only microscopic structures resembling red blood cells preserved within the dinosaur bone, but also chemical evidence of heme — a molecule in hemoglobin, the protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen.

stories.excerpt: An adviser to the European Union’s top court said Tuesday that Google’s artificial intelligence chatbot Gemini may be breaking copyright rules in certain cases when it uses press publications. Using material for training an AI model is “freely permitted under the text and data mining exception,” Advocate General Maciej Szpunar, an adviser to the court who issues a legal opinion before judges rule, said. But he noted there was “no evidence that Like Company’s articles” had been used to train Gemini. It is the first generative AI case, involving systems that create text and other content, to reach the European Court of Justice, after Hungarian press publisher Like Company took Google to court over the use of articles from its online news portals. stories.excerpt: CNN’s Election Night coverage has for decades featured the results of surveys, known as exit polls that aim to explain how and why voters made their decisions. This year, those surveys are changing and they have a new name. The CNN Voter Poll incorporates traditional in-person exit polling techniques alongside a robust, large-sample nationwide survey fielded before Election Day. The two sample sources combined will yield an in-depth look at the electorate nationally as well as in the 45 states holding US Senate or governor elections this midterm. "Interception and destruction of a drone in the Mecca region," Turki al-Malki, the coalition's spokesperson wrote on social media, without elaborating on the source of the attack. The interception came a day after the coalition said that it had intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile and two drones fired by the Houthis toward Saudi territory. Mecca is home to one of Islam's holiest sites, the Kabba, which draws millions of pilgrims every year, making it a red line for Saudi Arabia and the Muslim world in general. The development follows escalating hostilities between the Houthi group and the Saudi-led coalition, which supports Yemen's internationally recognized government. stories.title: Bangladesh garment workers wage protests enter 4th day
stories.description: Bangladesh police fired tear gas Tuesday to disperse garment workers on their fourth day of wage protests, which have disrupted factories and transport in the nation's vital export...
stories.excerpt: Bangladesh police fired tear gas Tuesday to disperse garment workers on their fourth day of wage protests, which have disrupted factories and transport in the nation's vital export sector. The unrest, which began Saturday, has intensified despite the government's move to form a six-member wage board to review pay in Bangladesh's garment sector, the world's second-largest apparel exporter after China. This comes at a critical time for manufacturers entering the peak production season for spring and summer export orders. The industry employs about 4 million workers, supplies global brands such as H&M, Zara and Gap, and accounts for more than 80% of the country's export earnings. Clashes were reported across industrial belts around Dhaka, including Ashulia, Gazipur and the capital's Mirpur area, as workers staged fresh demonstrations and attempted to block major highways. stories.excerpt: King Charles III and Queen Camilla were caught in heavy rain as they attended Independence Day celebrations in Antigua and Barbuda on Sunday, November 1. The royal couple sat alongside Prime Minister Gaston Browne at Sir Vivian Richards Stadium, where they were greeted by Governor-General Rodney Williams ahead of a ceremony recognising citizens for their contributions to national development. The visit coincides with Antigua and Barbuda hosting the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) from November 1 to 4, bringing leaders together to discuss investment, development and international cooperation. The Caribbean nation gained independence from Britain on November 1, 1981.

stories.excerpt: Russian overnight strikes pummeled Ukraine on Tuesday, according to authorities, as renewed fighting dimmed prospects for peace in the nearly five-year war. Strikes across the country killed dozens, forced medical facility evacuations and triggered a wave of ballistic missile alerts. In Russia, Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said air defenses destroyed nearly 500 drones heading toward the capital region. The attacks followed a rare pause in the fighting between Russia and Ukraine in the southern Ukrainian region of Kherson, which ended Sunday. The truce, the longest of the war that began in February 2022, enabled a humanitarian mission to the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky. Hours after the local cease-fire ended, Russia targeted a village in Ukraine's southeastern Zaporizhzhia region, killing at least 26 people, the acting regional governor said. stories.title: Russian drone attacks turn the Black Sea into the world’s deadliest waterway
stories.description: Russian drones have struck at least a dozen merchant ships in the Black Sea in recent weeks – killing more mariners than have died during the Iran war.
stories.excerpt: Russian drones have struck at least a dozen merchant ships in the Black Sea in recent weeks – killing more mariners than have died during the Iran war. Russia’s goal is to throttle trade through Ukrainian ports, which export almost all the country’s grain. But some attacks have occurred close to or inside the territorial waters of two NATO states: Romania and Bulgaria. The Russian campaign follows months of Ukrainian strikes on ships using Russian ports in the Black Sea and adjoining Sea of Azov – and has accelerated over the past month. On several occasions, according to shipping and security sources, Russia has combined maritime and aerial drones. It has begun using recently developed jet-powered drones, which are faster and more difficult to intercept, as well as drones capable of hitting moving targets. stories.excerpt: The US military carried out limited strikes on Iran’s Qeshm Island on Monday, three US officials told CNN, characterizing the action as defensive in nature and meant to protect US assets in the region. One official said the US attack came in response to Iran firing at a US aircraft. It does not appear to be the kind of major combat operation that officials have been contemplating, and the Wall Street Journal, which first revealed the operation, reported that other such strikes have been carried out previously in secret. “This was a defensive measure for Iranians using surface-to-air missiles against US assets,” another US official said. But the new action, on the eve of Election Day, is a reminder that the situation in Iran is still unresolved, and combat is still very much on the table.
